hero_kpi_rationale: Stable revenue despite a challenging environment marked by contractual issues in the UK. The group maintains a solid revenue base of £8.44 billion across its three main divisions: Construction Services, Support Services, and Infrastructure Investments.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company through its core operations.
kpis.description: Total revenue includes joint ventures and associates, reflecting the group's overall activity.
kpis.signal: Revenue stability despite a difficult environment.

kpis.name: Profit from Continuing Operations
kpis.explanation: Pre-tax result from core operations, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Underlying profit was negative in 2014, impacted by problematic contracts in the UK, compared to £131 million in 2013.

kpis.name: Net Cash
kpis.explanation: Available cash after repayment of short-term debt, before non-recourse infrastructure concessions.
kpis.description: Net cash position of £219 million in 2014 versus a net debt position of £66 million in 2013, indicating prudent capital management prior to infrastructure concessions.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in liquidity due to internal transformation and capital management.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Global workforce of 36,000 employees reflects the group's operational scale across key markets: UK, North America, Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount paid to shareholders per share held.
kpis.description: Dividend per share was 5.6 pence in 2014 versus 14.1 pence in 2013. The final dividend was not recommended in 2014 to strengthen the balance sheet, but the group expects to reinstate the dividend at an appropriate level by March 2016.
kpis.signal: Significant dividend reduction due to weak performance.

risks.title: Failures in control and project risk management
risks.score_rationale: Dominant risk mentioned in the Chairman's Review title ("a challenging and redefining year"). Highly intense language: "failures of risk management", "control environment was not effective", "poor control over projects". Trend UP: issues identified in 2012-2013, worsened in 2014 with £281m in losses. Category weight very high: affects 70% of revenue according to the CEO.

risks.title: Concentration risk on problematic legacy contract portfolio
risks.score_rationale: Central position in Item 1A and Chairman's Review. Urgent language: "legacy contracts", "substantial write-downs" (£118m additional in 2014). Trend UP: problems extending beyond 2014. Category weight critical: majority of 45 problematic contracts expected completed by end-2015, but "major challenges remain".

risks.title: Excessive organizational complexity and acquisition integration
risks.score_rationale: Identified as root cause by CEO: "rapid fourfold revenue expansion since 2000, largely by acquisitions which were insufficiently integrated". Clear language: "overly complex, devolved organisation with poor controls". Trend STABLE but recognized as structural issue. Category weight high: affects governance and overall controls.

risks.title: Structural cost overruns and excessive cost base
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly quantified: "Group-wide overheads approximately 1% of revenue above industry benchmarks". Direct CEO statement: "cost base of the Group is too high". Trend STABLE but recognized as systemic issue. Category weight high: affects competitiveness and margins.

risks.title: Dependence on stabilization of Investments portfolio
risks.score_rationale: Important in strategy: "Investments portfolio provides an important anchor to the Group's balance sheet and profits". Moderate but strategic language. Trend UP: value increased from £766m (2013) to £1.3bn (2014). Category weight medium: 7% of revenue but critical for financial stability.

risks.title: Health and safety risks and operational fatigue
risks.score_rationale: Tragic event: 6 worker fatalities in 2014. Serious language: "There is renewed focus on fatal risks". Trend UP: shift in primary KPI to Lost Time Injury Rate, launch of "Zero Harm" programs. Category weight high: operating license non-negotiable.

risks.title: Dependence on UK construction market stabilization
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Chairman's Review: "I remain convinced that all our operations can achieve industry-standard performance as markets improve". Conditional language. Trend STABLE: market recovering but persistent uncertainty. Category weight medium: UK = 50% of revenue.

risks.title: Risk of managerial transformation and executive continuity
risks.score_rationale: Major changes: CEO Andrew McNaughton resigned May 2014, Leo Quinn appointed January 2015, CFO Duncan Magrath departs May 2015, Chairman Steve Marshall departs March 2015. Language: "substantial people changes". Trend UP: high turnover. Category weight medium: affects strategic continuity.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the 2014 annual report. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation.
Absence of products or services related to digital technology.
Strategy focused on operational transformation and contract management.
